lessons: Lead immediately with an extraordinary comparison or high-stakes historical/scale fact (e.g., 'older than the United States' yielded 1.85x retention at 10% and >1.0 at the end).
Never repeat the video title or basic premise as the opening line; verbatim title repetition caused immediate drops of 31.9% (Potatoes) and 34.0% (Garlic).
Avoid artificial 'pause and guess' prompts and interactive countdowns, which consistently triggered sharp viewer drop-offs (e.g., 15.2% loss on the foil video countdown line).
Establish clear visual or physical contrasts upfront (e.g., tuna vs. cod meat retained 65.8% at 50% mark) rather than starting with abstract definitions or setup statements.
Deliver the core scientific mechanism quickly; viewers abandon videos early when presented with verbose or multi-clause explanations in the first 15 seconds.
worst_moment_types: Verbatim restatement of the title or video topic at the start
Interactive pauses and countdown prompts ('Pause and guess...')
Dense, multi-clause explanatory setups right after the hook
Generic filler lines restating obvious observations ('They look like similar fruits')
best_hook_types: Historical or temporal scale anchors ('older than the United States')
Challenging established boundaries or paradigms ('Pluto seemed like our solar system's edge...')
Direct visual paradoxes and strong sensory contrasts ('both fish, but their meat looks like two completely different animals')
Surprising mystery framing ('Most James Webb images hold secrets')
